items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: We did a tour with Sweets and Buck Clayton in Europe. It was called “The Count’s Men” — it was all the old Basie alumni. And Freddie Green was there and Nat played Count’s part, I played the drums

ctx.x: One of the guys said, “If he looked any sharper I’d be bleeding.”

He’s got a million of those, and some that I wouldn’t want to talk about here. But Sweets is great. And it was so much fun playing with him. He still has that great sense of time and swing. He doesn’t have to play a lot of notes. And tempo doesn’t bother him, anything. The only thing I noticed last night, which I haven’t worked with Sweets now for a couple of years. I haven’t been on the same stand with him. But I noticed he has to sit down now when he plays — he sits on a chair. I did a tour with Sweets and Buck…

Clayton in Europe. It was called “The Count’s Men” — it was all the old Basie alumni. And Freddie Green was there and Nat played Count’s part, I played the drums and Jo Jones, who was alive at the time, followed us around France. We did a month in France. And at that time he was ailing pretty badly.
